blocks.title: Head start (Fri to Sun)
blocks.goal: Tools ready, Python bridge done, first concurrent LLM script running before week 1.

tasks.text: Install Python 3.12+ and uv. Create a repo named genai-prep with a README. Put your LLM API key in a .env file and add .env to .gitignore. Make one successful API call from Python.
tasks.done_when: A script prints a model reply, and git status shows .env is ignored.

resources.title: uv: Python package and project manager

tasks.text: Type hints, dataclasses and Pydantic models. Read the Pydantic docs overview and models page, then write 3 models including a nested one.
tasks.done_when: A nested model validates good JSON and raises a readable error for bad JSON.

tasks.text: Generators, decorators, context managers. Read the two Real Python articles, then write @retry(times=3, backoff=2) and a timing decorator.
tasks.done_when: A test where a function fails twice then succeeds passes; the generator version of a 1 GB file reader uses constant memory.

resources.title: How to use generators and yield

tasks.text: async/await in practice. Read the Real Python walkthrough, then call 50 URLs with at most 5 in flight using asyncio.gather and a Semaphore.
tasks.done_when: You measured the sync vs async runtime and can explain the difference in one sentence.

resources.title: Async IO in Python: a complete walkthrough

tasks.text: HTTPX streaming and pytest. Stream a response and print chunks as they arrive. Write one pytest test that mocks the HTTP call.
tasks.done_when: Streaming prints tokens incrementally and the mocked test passes in under a second.

tasks.text: Concurrent prompt runner: send 50 prompts with retries, timeout and a rate limit. Print total cost and p50 and p95 latency.
tasks.done_when: One command runs 50 prompts; the output shows cost, p50 and p95; a failed call is retried and logged.

tasks.text: Wrap the runner in a FastAPI endpoint with Pydantic request and response models.
tasks.done_when: POST /run returns validated JSON; invalid input returns a 422 with a clear message.

tasks.text: Push to GitHub with a README. List the three Python features that were new to you.
tasks.done_when: Repo is public or shareable; README says how to run it.

blocks.title: Week 1: Prompting, structured outputs, tool calling
blocks.goal: Ship an extraction API that turns messy documents into validated JSON, with a 50-case eval.

tasks.text: Solve: Two Sum; Contains Duplicate. Pattern: hash map.
tasks.done_when: For each problem you named the pattern, stated time and space complexity aloud and tested one edge case. Anything you could not finish in 30 minutes goes on the redo list for Sunday.

tasks.text: Prompt anatomy. Read the Anthropic prompt engineering overview (30 min), do the first chapters of the interactive tutorial (45 min), then skim OpenAI's guide for differences (15 min).
tasks.done_when: One task written five ways (zero-shot, few-shot, with a role, with XML-style structure, with reasoning) in one file, with a note on which won.

tasks.text: Solve: Valid Anagram; Group Anagrams. Pattern: hash map.
tasks.done_when: For each problem you named the pattern, stated time and space complexity aloud and tested one edge case. Anything you could not finish in 30 minutes goes on the redo list for Sunday.

tasks.done_when: Name, date and amount are extracted into a Pydantic model; invalid output triggers one retry that includes the validation error text.

tasks.text: Solve: Top K Frequent Elements; Product of Array Except Self. Pattern: hash map + heap, prefix/suffix.
tasks.done_when: For each problem you named the pattern, stated time and space complexity aloud and tested one edge case. Anything you could not finish in 30 minutes goes on the redo list for Sunday.

tasks.text: Tool calling end to end. Read the tool-use docs, then build a calculator tool and a lookup tool and run the full loop.
tasks.done_when: Model calls a tool, you execute it, send the result back, and the final answer is correct on 5 test questions; unknown tools and bad arguments return a clear error to the model.

tasks.text: Solve: Valid Sudoku; Longest Consecutive Sequence. Pattern: hash set.
tasks.done_when: For each problem you named the pattern, stated time and space complexity aloud and tested one edge case. Anything you could not finish in 30 minutes goes on the redo list for Sunday.

tasks.text: Context management. Read Anthropic's context engineering post and the prompt caching docs. Skim 'Lost in the Middle'. Use Tiktokenizer to count tokens.
tasks.done_when: A function trims chat history to a token budget; you measured latency or cost with caching on a repeated long prefix.

resources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

tasks.text: Implement a token-bucket rate limiter and an exponential backoff with jitter scheduler, with tests. Then solve Valid Palindrome.
tasks.done_when: Limiter allows N calls per second under a burst test; backoff delays grow and are randomized; tests pass.

tasks.text: Eval basics. Read Hamel Husain's two evals posts. Write a 50-case JSONL dataset for your extractor and a scoring script.
tasks.done_when: Dataset has inputs and expected fields; the script prints per-field accuracy.

resources.title: LLM Evals: everything you need to know

tasks.text: Extraction API v1: FastAPI POST /extract with a Pydantic schema, retries on invalid output and an async batch endpoint.
tasks.done_when: 10 documents processed in one batch call; invalid outputs retried once; every response validates against the schema.

tasks.text: Collect and label 50 real documents (invoices, emails or resumes with personal data removed) as ground truth.
tasks.done_when: 50 labeled JSON files in a data folder with a README line describing the labeling rules.

tasks.text: Eval harness: run all 50 documents, report field-level accuracy, p50 and p95 latency and cost per document. Put the first numbers in the README.
tasks.done_when: make eval prints a table you can paste into the README.

resources.title: A Field Guide to Rapidly Improving AI Products

tasks.text: Write a byte-pair-encoding trainer: count adjacent pairs on a 1,000-word corpus, merge the most frequent pair 50 times, then encode new text. Then solve Valid Parentheses.

tasks.text: ML basics for interviews. Read the scikit-learn metrics page and watch StatQuest on ROC/AUC and cross-validation. Drill 10 questions.

tasks.text: Implement scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention in PyTorch. Verify against nn.MultiheadAttention.

resources.title: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out

tasks.text: Implement temperature, top-k and top-p sampling in NumPy and plot the distributions.
tasks.done_when: A plot shows the distribution before and after each filter.

tasks.text: RAG v0: embed 200 chunks with a sentence-embedding model, store vectors, search by cosine similarity and answer with a citation.
tasks.done_when: A question returns the right chunk in the top 3 on 10 hand-picked questions.

tasks.text: Tidy RAG v0 into a repo with FAISS or NumPy search, a script to ingest files and a README.
tasks.done_when: Fresh clone runs ingest and a sample question in under 5 minutes.

tasks.text: Transformer and ML-basics questions. Record yourself explaining the transformer in two minutes.
tasks.done_when: Answer each question aloud in under 90 seconds without notes. Mark the ones where you hesitated and re-answer them on Wednesday.
questions: Explain self-attention step by step. Why scale by the square root of d_k?
Why multi-head attention instead of one big head?
Encoder-only, decoder-only and encoder-decoder: when would you use each?

What is the KV cache, why does it speed up generation, and what does it cost?
Why is attention O(n^2) and how do FlashAttention and grouped-query attention help?
How does BPE work? What happens to words the vocabulary has never seen?
What do temperature, top-k and top-p each do?
Precision vs recall: give a case where each matters more. Why is accuracy misleading on imbalanced data?
What is data leakage? Give three examples and how you would prevent each.
